_about: Aristotle in English: the Oxford translation, The Works of Aristotle Translated into English, ed. J. A. Smith and W. D. Ross (Oxford: Clarendon, 1908-1952, 12 vols.). Raw Internet Archive OCR, one item per volume (mostly the St. Michael's College, Toronto set, which follows the official numbering), translator recorded per work. Bekker pages are printed in the margins and survive in the OCR; nothing is converted yet (the Edwards precedent). Rights: US public domain for volumes published 1930 or earlier (vols. I, II, IV-XI). Vol. III (1931) enters the US public domain on 2027-01-01 and Vol. XII (1952) is not cleared, so neither is fetched; its pre-1931 parts (Meteorologica 1923, De Mundo 1914, Parva Naturalia 1908) want genuine separate issues, not yet found, and a PD 1902 English De Anima + Parva Naturalia (Hammond) stands in as a gap-fill. Several translators died after 1956, so these are not public domain in the UK or other life+70 countries. English only; no Greek (Perseus Greek not pulled). Clean Gutenberg witnesses (rows ending -pg): Butcher's and Bywater's Poetics, Kenyon's Athenian Constitution, Cresswell's History of Animals. Ellis's Politics and Chase's Ethics are on the Adler shelf and Edghill's Categories is in vol. I (see _held). Added 2026-10-03, older single-work translations (raw IA unless noted): Taylor's Metaphysics (1801); the Bohn volumes of Browne (Ethics, 1850), Owen (Organon, 1853, 2 vols.) and the literal Rhetoric with Buckley's Poetic (1857); Peters's Ethics (1881); Welldon's Politics (1883, in a 1901 printing), Rhetoric (1886) and Ethics (1892); and from Gutenberg, Ellis's Politics and the Everyman Ethics (translator unnamed in the file). Added 2026-10-03 (later): John H. M'Mahon's literal Metaphysics (Bohn, 1857), raw IA OCR (Google scan; the title page prints the name M'Mahon). Also Edward Walford's Politics and Economics (Bohn, 1853); his preface says the Politics is based on Ellis's version, revised against Taylor and Gillies. Perseus TEI English (section "perseus", fetched by pipeline/fetch_perseus.py): the translations are public domain; the TEI markup is Perseus Digital Library's, CC BY-SA 4.0 (attribution and share-alike), and each file's own licence statement and a rights block (license, attribution, source_url, share_alike, redistribute_whole false) are recorded per row in _perseus_checks and in the shelf's perseus report.

_excluded.vol. III (1931): Meteorologica (Webster), De Mundo (Forster), De Anima (J. A. Smith), Parva Naturalia (Beare and Ross), De Spiritu (Dobson). Published 1931: US public domain from 2027-01-01. Pending; IA has worksofaristotle03arisuoft ready
_excluded.vol. XII (1952): Select Fragments (Ross). Published 1952; renewal status not checked; not cleared. Pending
_excluded.worksofaristotle10arisuoft / 11 / 12: duplicate Toronto scans of vols. X-XII; the 'theworksofaristo' scans kept
_excluded.R. D. Hicks, De Anima (1907): PD and a fine translation, but printed with the Greek text facing; Greek-English mixed OCR. Pending as an alternative De Anima
_excluded.Perseus English Aristotle: Loeb translations (Rackham, Tredennick, Freese); thin and not the Oxford corpus. Gap-fill only if a hole remains; none fetched Update 2026-10-03: Rackham's Nicomachean Ethics (Loeb, 1926 printing) taken as a second Ethics witness (aristotle-perseus-rackham-nicomachean-ethics); Freese's Rhetoric refused (1947 printing in its record).
_excluded.worksofaristotle00unse (1830): 'Aristotle's Masterpiece', a popular sex-and-midwifery manual falsely ascribed to Aristotle. Wrong author
_excluded.meteorologica00aris: Catalogued as 'Meteorologica, 1923, separate issue', but the scan is the whole of vol. III as bound in 1931: it carries J. A. Smith's De Anima, first published 1931. Checked by its sub-title pages (1923, 1914, 1931, 1908). Removed after fetching; pending with vol. III until 2027-01-01. The PD parts (Meteorologica 1923, De Mundo 1914, Parva Naturalia 1908) want genuine separate issues
_excluded.tlg0086.tlg038.perseus-eng2: Freese's Loeb Rhetoric (1926) on Perseus: the file's sourceDesc gives a 1947 printing, and the gate refused it because no reason was written. It is in the same position as the kept Aeschines and Isaeus printings, so it is put to Adam with that whole class in DIGEST-B; held back until he rules. The Bohn Rhetoric is held meanwhile
